ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are 9 squares arranged horizontally in one row. Counting from left to right, the 5th square has already been filled with 3, the 7th square has already been filled with 1, and the remaining squares are empty. Reasoning: Denote the 9 squares from left to right as x1,x2,...,x9, then the figure gives x5=3, x7=1. The condition is that the sum of any three consecutive numbers is a multiple of 3, that is xi+x{i+1}+x{i+2}≡0 (mod 3), i=1,...,7. Subtracting two adjacent congruences of three consecutive sums gives x{i+3}≡xi (mod 3). Therefore the numbers in positions 1,4,7 are congruent modulo 3; the numbers in positions 2,5,8 are congruent modulo 3; the numbers in positions 3,6,9 are congruent modulo 3. Because x7=1, positions 1,4,7 must contain the numbers with remainder 1 modulo 3, {1,4,7}, among which 1 has already been fixed in the 7th square, so positions 1 and 4 have 2! ways to be filled. Because x5=3, positions 2,5,8 must contain the numbers with remainder 0 modulo 3, {3,6,9}, among which 3 has already been fixed in the 5th square, so positions 2 and 8 have 2! ways to be filled. The remaining positions 3,6,9 contain the numbers with remainder 2 modulo 3, {2,5,8}, with 3! ways to be filled. Therefore the total number is 2!*2!*3!=24.
